verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b, and two committers who know pgstat asked for the fixed array. Two fixable level 2 points remain. maintenance-fit-1 asks for query-latency numbers for the array version, because the thread only measured the dshash version. standards-compat-1 asks what a shared reset does to each live entry's stats_reset.

brief.title: Redesign per-backend statistics with ProcNumber-indexed shared arrays
brief.problem: Per-backend WAL, lock and I/O statistics are reported and stored twice, once in the global fixed statistics and once in PGSTAT_KIND_BACKEND. Reviewers raised this duplicated work, and its cost grows as more statistics gain per-backend reporting. The current design also excludes auxiliary processes such as the checkpointer, background writer, startup process and autovacuum launcher.
brief.proposed_design: Each participating fixed-numbered kind keeps a shared accumulator for exited processes plus a ProcNumber-indexed shared array, sized at startup, for live processes, each entry with its own LWLock. Flushes update only the live entry, global views add all live entries to the accumulator, and entries move into the accumulator at exit, ProcNumber reuse and clean shutdown. WAL, lock and I/O move over, and PGSTAT_KIND_BACKEND is removed.
user_visible_surface: pg_stat_get_backend_wal(), pg_stat_get_backend_lock() and pg_stat_get_backend_io() now return rows for the checkpointer, background writer, startup process, autovacuum launcher and shared-memory-only workers.
pg_stat_reset_shared('wal'), ('lock') and ('io') now also clear the per-backend statistics of every live process.
Queries on pg_stat_wal, pg_stat_lock and pg_stat_io now add up all live per-backend entries, so they cost more with many backends.
PgStat_KindInfo gains per-backend metadata, and registering a custom statistics kind with per-backend entries fails with an error.
PGSTAT_KIND_BACKEND is removed, and pgstat_backend.c now holds the generic per-backend infrastructure.
author_claims: Each counter is reported and stored once.
Flushes no longer take the global statistics lock or do a hash lookup, which removes global lock contention from the flush path.
WAL, lock and I/O get independent storage and locking, so adding a new per-backend statistic adds no contention to existing kinds.
With 5000 maximum backends the fixed array takes about 16 MB; the earlier dshash version used 22 MB with 3735 sessions.
In the dshash version, global view queries went from about 0.02-0.07 ms to 0.35-2.8 ms at 10000 backends; the author calls this acceptable.
brief.thread_state: Michael Paquier and Andres Freund pushed for a fixed array over dshash, and v4 adopted it; v5 addresses Michael's review of v4. Open items are whether to keep the snapshot TAP test and when to support custom per-backend statistics, which the author leaves for a follow-up.
unclear: The thread gives no query-latency numbers for the fixed-array version, only for the dshash version.
The thread gives no flush-path benchmark showing reduced lock contention against master.
The proposal does not say how much shared memory is used at common max_connections values, or whether it scales with max_worker_processes and other process slots.
The thread does not say whether monitoring tools that rely on per-backend counters surviving a shared reset need a release note.

prior_attempts.title: Get rid of pgstat_count_backend_io_op*() functions
prior_attempts.quote: Hmm. I really have an issue with the ordering dependency this introduces between stats kinds, assumed to happen inside the code.
prior_attempts.reason: Michael Paquier objected to the ordering dependency between stats kinds at flush time, which so far have been independent, and said the copy approach hurts readability. He also said there was no benchmark data to choose among inlining, static structures, copies or fewer diffs, so the picture was incomplete. Andres Freund rejected the alternative WalUsage-style diff approach as too costly. The thread ends with the author disagreeing, and the visible messages do not show a final decision.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: Both remove the double counting of per-backend I/O, but P1 copied pending I/O stats into the backend kind and needed a flush order between kinds. Here each kind owns its own ProcNumber-indexed entries, so no copy and no flush ordering remain.

objections.title: Global view query cost scales with MaxBackends, unmeasured for the array design
objections.failure_scenario: A site with max_connections = 5000 runs a monitoring agent that polls pg_stat_io every few seconds on each node. Every query now takes one shared LWLock per array slot and adds up every entry. The operator sees higher monitoring latency, and more time spent in LWLock calls, only after upgrading.
objections.argument: The only latency numbers are for the dshash version (message #5), where pg_stat_io went from about 0.07 ms to 2.8 ms at 10000 backends. Message #10 says a fixed array must also visit unused slots, and the v4/v5 array design has no numbers at all. pg_stat_io, pg_stat_wal and pg_stat_lock are read by nearly every monitoring tool, so the cost falls on everyone, including people who never call pg_stat_get_backend_*(). Each later per-backend kind adds another scan of this kind.
objections.author_must_show: What do pg_stat_io, pg_stat_wal and pg_stat_lock cost with v5 at a few common max_connections values, with most slots idle or unused, compared with master?

critic.reasoning: The thread's only latency numbers are for the dshash version, and the array version scans every slot. The claim of one LWLock per unused slot is not established, and two committers who know the area asked for the array, so this is a request for numbers.

objections.title: Shared reset now clears live per-backend counters without a stated contract
objections.failure_scenario: A monitoring agent samples pg_stat_get_backend_io() for each pid and graphs deltas. A DBA runs pg_stat_reset_shared('io'), and every live backend's counters drop to zero. Unless the per-backend stats_reset timestamp also changes, the agent reports negative or wrapped deltas and finds out only from wrong graphs after upgrade.
objections.argument: On master, a shared reset leaves per-backend counters alone, and pg_stat_reset_backend_stats() resets them. The doc hunks in 0003-0005 add the new reach of pg_stat_reset_shared() but do not say whether each live entry's stats_reset is updated. Message #1 calls this "a documented behavior change", but the thread has no release-note text and no rule for how clients tell a shared reset from a per-backend one. Tools that already use the per-backend functions upgrade into this silently.
objections.author_must_show: After pg_stat_reset_shared('io'), does each live backend's per-backend stats_reset change, and what release-note text tells tool authors about the new reset reach?

critic.reasoning: The doc hunks in 0003-0005 state the new reset reach, but nothing says whether each live entry's stats_reset changes after a shared reset. The release-note request should be dropped, because Postgres patches do not carry release-note text, and backpatching does not apply.

questions: What do pg_stat_io, pg_stat_wal and pg_stat_lock cost with v5 at a few common max_connections values, with most slots unused, compared with master?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier reviews the series in the visible thread, and the commit messages list him and Andres Freund as reviewers; both asked for the fixed array.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the correctness of global totals across process exit, ProcNumber reuse and clean shutdown, for the query cost of three widely polled views, and for the changed reset behaviour, for as long as the cumulative statistics code lives.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted five versions in about three months and changed the design from dshash to a fixed array after review, which suggests he stays for fixes.

priority.reason: The series removes duplicate accounting that reviewers raised and unblocks further per-backend statistics, and committers who know pgstat are engaged. Six staged patches stay within the pgstat code, and the two open points need numbers and one documented answer.

provisional_note: Without the code, the locking on unused slots and the transfer at exit, ProcNumber reuse and shutdown could not be checked for lost or double-counted counters. Only 3 of 15 messages were shown, so some open questions may already have answers in the thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: Get rid of pgstat_count_backend_io_op*() functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the pgstat_count_backend_io_op*() functions, so I/O counters are incremented once, and copies the pending I/O stats into the per-backend pending stats when the I/O stats flush. To make this work, per-backend stats must flush after the other stats kinds, first by placing PGSTAT_KIND_BACKEND last in the enum and later (v3) by flushing it outside the loop in pgstat_report_stat().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected to the ordering dependency between stats kinds at flush time, which so far have been independent, and said the copy approach hurts readability. He also said there was no benchmark data to choose among inlining, static structures, copies or fewer diffs, so the picture was incomplete. Andres Freund rejected the alternative WalUsage-style diff approach as too costly. The thread ends with the author disagreeing, and the visible messages do not show a final decision.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Hmm.  I really have an issue with the ordering dependency this
introduces between stats kinds, assumed to happen inside the code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve management of SLRU statistics collection.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Improve management of SLRU statistics collection.
Reverted commit(s): Move each SLRU's lwlocks to a separate tranche.; Collect statistics about SLRU caches
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Instead of re-identifying which statistics bucket to use for a given
SLRU on every counter increment, do it once during shmem initialization.
This saves a fair number of cycles, and there's no real cost because
we could not have a bucket assignment that varies over time or across
backends anyway.

Also, get rid of the ill-considered decision to let pgstat.c pry
directly into SLRU's shared state; it's cleaner just to have slru.c
pass the stats bucket number.

In consequence of these changes, there's no longer any need to store
an SLRU's LWLock tranche info in shared memory, so get rid of that,
making this a net reduction in shmem consumption.  (That partly
reverts fe702a7b3.)

This is basically code review for 28cac71bd, so I also cleaned up
some comments, removed a dangling extern declaration, fixed some
things that should be static and/or const, etc.

precedents_retrieved.title: Show WAL stats on pg_stat_io
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds WAL I/O (writes, fsyncs, reads during recovery, and WAL segment initialization in a new IOCONTEXT_INIT) to the pg_stat_io view as IOOBJECT_WAL. Timings use track_wal_io_timing, and pg_stat_wal timings would come from pg_stat_io.
precedents_retrieved.objection: pg_stat_io ties op_bytes to a fixed block size per object and context, but some WAL reads, such as those by the WAL receiver, have a variable size. Reviewers did not agree whether to set op_bytes to 1, to NULL, or to add per-operation byte columns. Michael Paquier proposed to set the patch aside until WAL reads and writes, async I/O and cached reads are settled, so that the meaning of pg_stat_io does not change between releases. The author agreed, and the patch was marked Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IMHO, perhaps we'd better put this patch aside until we are absolutely
*sure* of what we want to achieve when it comes to WAL, and I am
afraid that this cannot happen until we're happy with the way we
handle WAL reads *and* writes, including WAL receiver or anything that
has the idea of pulling its own page callback with
XLogReaderAllocate() in the backend.

precedents_retrieved.title: WAL-logging facility for pgstats kinds
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a new "PgStat" resource manager and a pgstat_xlog_data() entry point so that any pgstats kind, including custom ones, can WAL-log its own stats data. Each kind handles replay through a redo callback in PgStat_KindInfo, so it can decide how the data persists on standbys and after crash recovery.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that stats only make sense on a replica or after a crash when they cover changes that are already WAL-logged, so they should be rebuilt during replay from the WAL records of the underlying objects. For table stats he proposed keying relation stats by relfilenode. He repeated the objection when the entry moved to the next CF, and the author then withdrew the patch and kept it aside.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I can't think of a real case where we would want to WAL log the stats
themselves, rather than re-emitting stats during replay based on the WAL
record of the "underlying object".

precedents_retrieved.title: Add tracking of backend memory allocated to pg_stat_activity
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a column to pg_stat_activity that shows the bytes of memory currently allocated by each backend, updated as memory contexts malloc and free memory. Dynamic shared memory counts only for the backend that created it, and the value cannot go below zero.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry to merge it into the thread "Add the ability to limit the amount of memory that can be allocated to backends", where it continued as patch 0001. Justin Pryzby suggested closing this entry once the patches moved there. The thread did not reject the design. Earlier comments about widening pg_stat_activity and about accuracy were still open when the entry closed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Flush pgstats file during checkpoints
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch writes the pgstats file during non-shutdown checkpoints and restart points and stores the checkpoint redo LSN in the file. At startup, including crash recovery, stats load when the redo LSN matches, so statistics survive a crash.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas found that stats entries can leak into the pgstats file after a crash, for example for a relation created in an uncommitted transaction. Since 5891c7a8ed nothing garbage-collects such orphaned entries. He also found that two immediate shutdowns in a row log an incorrect redo LSN warning, because the stats file is not flushed at the end-of-recovery checkpoint. Michael Paquier said he would look at these, and the visible messages end there.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: There are various race conditions where a stats entry can be leaked in the pgstats file.

precedents_retrieved.title: s/shm_mq_iovec/struct iovec/
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace the shm_mq module's own shm_mq_iovec struct with the standard POSIX struct iovec. The motivation was to remove a duplicate definition now that struct iovec can be used everywhere.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas argued that the two structs belong to separate APIs and should stay separate. Reusing struct iovec could tie shm_mq to POSIX limits such as IOV_MAX, and it would stop shm_mq from adding its own fields later. The author accepted this and marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
They serve a similar purpose,
but they belong to completely separate APIs; I think "incidental
deduplication" is the right term for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: pgstattuple: add test for coverage
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds SQL statements to the pgstattuple regression tests to raise code coverage from 50.6% to 78.7%. The tests insert data and check full `select *` output from the pgstattuple functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The tests added a dependency from pgstattuple on the bloom module, which Tom Lane objected to. The expected output also depended on platform details and failed on 32-bit systems. The author said he would fix it, but no updated version was posted, so Andres Freund marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: You definitely can't rely on such details not to change across platforms.

precedents_retrieved.title: Rather than mmap()-ing in 8k pages, mmap()'ing entire files into a backend.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Rather than mmap()-ing in 8k pages, mmap()'ing entire files into a backend.

precedents_retrieved.objection: Doing I/O to large tables would consume a lot of address space or require frequent mapping/unmapping. Extending the file also causes mapping problems that might require mapping only individual pages, leading to thousands of mappings. Another problem is that there is no way to _prevent_ I/O to disk from the dirty shared buffers so changes could hit disk before WAL is written.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

roaster_notes.note: The one related attempt, P1, failed on a flush-order dependency between stats kinds, and this design has no such dependency. Message #1 cites the earlier discussion that raised the double counting, and message #14 says the current design blocks new per-backend stats, so the thread itself starts from that history.
Other user-visible changes look compatible: per-backend rows for auxiliary processes only add data, and the custom-kind registration error blocks a feature that does not exist today.

The proposal adds no on-disk format change, WAL record, replication state, catalog change or protocol message, and no persistent state outside the stats file. Live entries move into the global accumulators before a clean shutdown writes the stats file, and crash recovery discards stats as before. The PgStat_KindInfo change is an extension API change for a major release only, with no backpatch planned.

No objection from the security angle. The proposal adds no new SQL function, privilege or GUC. The per-backend functions and global views keep their current access rules. The new rows for the checkpointer, background writer, startup process and autovacuum launcher hold counters that pg_stat_io already shows per backend type. pg_stat_reset_shared() keeps its existing privilege check; it now also clears live per-backend entries, and only callers who can already reset shared statistics can do that. The extra per-entry shared locking on global view queries is a cost question for the performance angle. Ordinary flushes use a conditional lock acquire, so an unprivileged reader does not block other backends' routine flushes. The material does not say who may call pg_stat_get_backend_*() for other users' backends, and it does not change that.

Both committers who know pgstat, Michael Paquier and Andres Freund, are engaged and chose the fixed array, so ownership and the basic design look settled. The patch series is staged, with tests first. The memory cost was accepted in message #13, and support for custom per-backend kinds is deferred as a follow-up.

No existing feature, extension or tool meets this need. The proposal replaces PGSTAT_KIND_BACKEND, so it does not add a second mechanism, and the reviewers in messages #8, #9 and #13 settled the choice of a fixed array over keeping that kind. [P1] tried a different fix for the same double counting and does not show an existing alternative.

No demand objection. The problem is internal: duplicate accounting in the stats system that reviewers flagged. Andres Freund proposed this design and Michael Paquier backs the fixed array (messages #1, #8, #9, #13), so the request comes from the people who would own the area. Missing flush-path and fixed-array query numbers belong to the performance angle.
